Theme

Latin word

ūncia

ūncia, ūnciae f.

noun, first declension

one twelfth

In this lexicon

  • twelfth

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 13.48.1: Caesar, opīnor, ex ūnciā; Hor. Ars 327; Traupman 355

  • ūncia hōrae: five minutes

    modern

Notes

  1. 1ūncia: long u (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). Bennett §52: “like ūnus”, from which Varro derives it (ūncia ab ūnō, LL 5.171; de Vaan s.v. ūnus). The Romance words (Italian oncia, Spanish onza) point to a short vowel in later Latin; Rosen, Language 40 (1964) 21–22, takes *oiniciā through *ūnciā, with a later shortening.

Examples

  • sī dē quīncūnce remōta est ūncia, quid superat? … — triēns. — eu! rem poteris servāre tuam. redit ūncia, quid fit? — sēmis

    If one twelfth is taken from five twelfths, what is left? — A third. — Well done! You’ll be able to look after your money. Put the twelfth back: what does it make? — A half.Hor. Ars 327–330
